headline: OSISKO METALS GASPÉ: 211M AT 0.59% CU — NEW HIGH-GRADE VECTOR 500M WEST OF RESOURCE POINTS TO OUT-OF-PIT EXPANSION IN QUÉBEC
snippet: Osisko Metals (TSX-V: OM) reported September 28 that drill hole GCU-26-046 at the historic Gaspé copper project in Québec returned 211.5 metres averaging 0.59% Cu, including a 28.5m high-grade interval at 2.31% Cu with 11.8 g/t Ag. The intercept sits 500 to 600 metres west of the current mineral resource — a structural vector that management says supports out-of-pit expansion on ground not yet included in any resource model. Gaspé was the largest copper producer in Canadian history and hosts a 2021 NI 43-101 resource of 3.1 billion pounds of copper; the new western extension result, combined with the high-grade sub-interval, is the most significant single drill hole at the project in the current campaign and opens a new target corridor for the 2027 resource update.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD CHARTS PATH TO 2 MILLION OZ/YR BY 2029 — POST-ORLA MERGER MAKES IT NORTH AMERICA'S NEW SENIOR GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: In its first post-close investor presentation at Mining Forum Americas on September 28, Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) outlined a production roadmap to 2 million ounces per year by 2029, up from approximately 1.1 million oz/yr today. The company now operates six North American gold complexes — four in Canada, one in California, one in Brazil — with more than 60% of production in Canada following the Orla Mining close. Management framed the Orla acquisition as a platform deal that provides both near-term production and long-term exploration upside at Camino Rojo in Mexico and Windfall in Québec. At the current gold price above $4,100/oz, the combined entity is generating operating margins management described as the highest in the company's history, and the presentation focused entirely on execution and cost containment rather than further M&A.

headline: THUNDER GOLD TOWER MOUNTAIN: 232.5M AT 0.450 G/T AU — DRILLED GRADE RUNNING 12.5% ABOVE RESOURCE MODEL IN ONTARIO BULK TONNAGE SYSTEM
snippet: Thunder Gold Corp. (TSX-V: TGOL) announced September 28 that drill hole TM-26-008 at Tower Mountain in northwestern Ontario returned 232.5 metres averaging 0.450 g/t Au, including 33.0 metres averaging 1.383 g/t Au. The 232.5m continuous gold intercept is in the bulk tonnage zone where average grades are tracking 12.5% above the geological model — a positive variance that will feed into an updated mineral resource estimate planned for Q1 2027. A second drill is collared on a parallel conductor 400 metres to the north. Thunder Gold is a TSXV junior with Tower Mountain as its sole asset; at current gold prices the widening of confirmed drill grades above model is a meaningful upside signal for the upcoming resource.

headline: URANIUM AT $90/LB WITH 70% OF UTILITY NEEDS UNCOVERED FOR 2027-28 — STRUCTURAL DEFICIT CASE INTACT DESPITE GOLD-DRIVEN SECTOR SELLOFF
snippet: With spot uranium trading at $89.85 to $90.05 per pound on September 28, InvestorIdeas argues the Monday precious metals selloff is creating a distraction from the uranium sector's unchanged supply-demand fundamentals: a 30 to 40 million pound per year structural deficit, utilities with 70% of their 2027-28 requirements still uncovered on long-term contracts, and limited new primary supply able to come online before 2028. The analysis identifies $99/lb as the next technical breakout trigger, above which several institutional price targets from $110 to $130/lb become the base case. For retail investors holding TSXV and ASX uranium juniors, the current price consolidation near $90 is framed as a buying window rather than a trend reversal in a structural bull market that is still in its early middle innings.

headline: POWER MINERALS MORRO DO FERRO: 88M AT 6.33% TREO — MAIDEN 10.7MT EXPLORATION TARGET AT HIGHEST-GRADE RARE EARTH INTERCEPT IN PROJECT HISTORY
snippet: Power Minerals Ltd reported drill results from its Morro do Ferro rare earth project in Brazil returning 88 metres at 6.33% total rare earth oxide — the highest-grade intercept in the project's history — alongside the release of a maiden exploration target of 10.7 million tonnes. Morro do Ferro sits in Minas Gerais state, a historically significant REE province; the 6.33% TREO grade at depth is substantially higher than the surface-level grades historically documented at the project and suggests a higher-grade core that the maiden resource target has only partially defined. With the China rare earth export framework set to expire November 10, 2026, Brazilian and Australian rare earth projects are attracting increased investor attention as ex-China processing and magnet supply chains try to qualify alternative feedstock.

headline: GOLD SANK 4% IN 24 HOURS — FIVE INSTITUTIONAL SIGNALS THAT SHOW THE STRUCTURAL BID HAS NOT BROKEN
snippet: GoldSilver.com's institutional signals digest for September 29 identifies five data points arguing that gold's 4% correction to $4,100/oz is a macro-driven fear trade rather than a structural trend reversal: ETF inflows remain positive for the 12th consecutive week; central bank buying is tracking at 950 tonnes annualised versus the five-year average of 480 tonnes; CFTC managed-money net long positioning has pulled back to a six-month low, clearing speculative excess; the gold-to-real-yield correlation has broken down, suggesting the oil-driven rate-hike narrative is temporary; and China's physical import pace implies year-end demand of 1,700 tonnes even with Golden Week reducing activity this week. The $4,100/oz area is identified as the key level where institutional accumulation has historically reloaded in the 2025-2026 bull run.

headline: QMINES DOUBLES DRILL PROGRAM TO 20,000M AT MT CHALMERS — COPPER-GOLD BARGE ASSAYS DUE IMMINENTLY AT QUEENSLAND PROJECT
snippet: QMines Ltd (ASX: QML) announced it has doubled its 2026 drill program at the Mt Chalmers copper-gold project in Queensland from 10,000m to 20,000m, with assays from the current barge drilling campaign expected imminently. Mt Chalmers is a historic VMS copper-gold-zinc deposit with a current mineral resource; the expanded drill program targets lateral extensions of the high-grade core and two new submarine VMS targets identified through recent VTEM geophysics. The program doubling was funded from existing cash, and management cited the results from the first half of the drill season as justifying the accelerated investment. For ASX copper investors, QML is a small-cap development story with near-term resource update catalysts.

headline: WGC WEEKLY SEP 28: CHINA GOLDEN WEEK REMOVES THE KEY SPOT BID — SHORT-TERM DEMAND GAP IN A LONG-TERM DEMAND STORY
snippet: The World Gold Council's Weekly Market Monitor for September 28 identifies China's Golden Week holiday period (October 1-7) as a structural factor in the current gold price weakness: Chinese institutional and retail gold buyers who account for a significant share of daily spot volume will be largely inactive for seven trading days, creating a short-term demand gap that amplifies the oil-driven macro selloff. The WGC notes that in each of the past four years, gold has dipped modestly in the week before and during Golden Week before recovering as Chinese buyers return; the 2024 return-from-holiday buying period saw gold rise 3.8% in the two weeks following Golden Week. The report flags ETF flows, central bank communication and PCE data as the three near-term catalysts most capable of bridging the Golden Week demand gap.

headline: GOLD $4,185 IS THE LINE IN THE SAND — TECHNICAL CASE FOR BULLS AND BEARS AFTER THE OIL-DRIVEN THREE-PERCENT SELLOFF
snippet: FX Leaders' September 28 gold price forecast identifies $4,185/oz as the critical technical pivot following Monday's oil-driven selloff to $4,148. A close below $4,185 and then $4,157 would open a measured move toward $4,050, where the 50-day moving average and a prior consolidation zone provide the next meaningful support. A recovery above $4,300 is required to signal the correction is over and the primary uptrend has resumed. The analysis distinguishes the current selloff as oil-and-rate-driven rather than fundamental — no change in mine supply, ETF flows remain positive, and central bank demand has not slowed — and argues the bull case remains intact as long as $4,050 holds.

headline: GOLD ROYALTY AT MINING FORUM AMERICAS: GROWTH WITHOUT NEW CAPITAL AS ROYALTY STREAMERS OUTPACE PRODUCERS IN THE BULL MARKET
snippet: Gold Royalty Corp. (NYSE American: GROY; TSX: GROY) used its Mining Forum Americas presentation on September 28 to outline a growth model that requires no additional equity dilution or capital allocation decisions — royalties already acquired will generate increasing cash flow as underlying mines move through construction and into production. The presentation came in a week when Wheaton Precious Metals closed a $4.3 billion streaming deal and Franco-Nevada acquired a $170 million royalty on the Bullabulling gold project in Western Australia, underscoring that the royalty-and-streaming model is attracting the largest transactions in the sector. For retail investors, the royalty model — diversified royalty income with no capital cost exposure — offers a way to participate in gold's bull market with lower operational risk than individual mine operators.

headline: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER DOMINATE THE WEEK — WHAT JUNIOR MINING INVESTORS NEED TO KNOW GOING INTO OCTOBER
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's weekly investor briefing covering the final week of September 2026 addresses the key questions for retail investors entering October: gold's 4% correction and whether the $4,100 level holds; copper's pullback from its September record of $6.83/lb COMEX amid China demand data and twin strike votes at Escondida and Centinela; silver's battle with the $60/oz floor; and the macro calendar ahead including PCE Wednesday and NFP Friday. The report frames October as a month with significant binary catalysts — strike outcomes at two of the world's largest copper mines, US inflation data that could reset Fed rate expectations, and a potential resumption of Chinese precious metals buying post-Golden Week — and recommends investors watch volume and positioning data rather than reacting to daily price moves in the current high-volatility period.
